data.gender_notes: Arafat is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A person who performs pilgrimage to the sacred place. The name Arafat carries the meaning “Pilgrimage” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Arafat usually hope their child will grow to embody pilgrimage and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Arafat belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Pilgrimage.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Arafat total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Arafat" holds immense significance in Islamic culture as it refers to the nearby hill in Saudi Arabia where Muslims perform an integral part of the Hajj pilgrimage - standing in contemplation and repentance before Allah. This annual congregation of millions of people not only strengthens bonding between Muslims but also fosters peace and unity amongst them.
data.spiritual_significance: The significance of the name "Arafat" inspires a deep spiritual recognition within every Muslim performing the Hajj pilgrimage. It represents a pivotal moment in their spiritual journey where they seek forgiveness for past sins, renew their faith, and prayerfully seek Allah's guidance for the future. This introspective moment of reflection and devotion ultimately leads to a purified soul and a stronger connection with Allah.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Pilgrimage" symbolizes A person who performs pilgrimage to the sacred place. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Arafat serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of pilgrimage.
